There is an asymmetry between commit/abort and preparation phase if the
following conditions are met:
1. set is a verdict map (""1.2.3.4 : jump foo"")
2. timeouts are enabled
In this case
1. element E in set S refers to chain C
2. userspace requests removal of set S
3. kernel does a set walk to decrement chain->use count for all elements
from preparation phase
4. kernel does another set walk to remove elements from the commit phase
(or another walk to do a chain->use increment for all elements from
abort phase)
If E has already expired in 1)
column2: it will be ignored during list walk

column1: won't have been changed.
Then
column3: ->destroy callback will zap the element via

column1: nf_tables_set_elem_destroy()
column2: but this function is only safe for

column1: elements that have been deactivated earlier from the preparation phase:
lack of earlier deactivate removes the element but leaks the chain use
count
column2: which results in a WARN splat when the chain gets removed later

column1: plus a leak of the nft_chain structure.
Update pipapo_get() not to skip expired elements
command reports bogus ENOENT errors.
